title: Macroecology of Microbial Performance Across Earth's Biomes
content:
ABSTRACT

Aim

A central goal of global ecology is to determine whether widespread spatial distribution reflects broad ecological performance. For microorganisms, this remains unresolved because occurrence and performance are rarely evaluated together across biomes. Here, we examine how global distribution and ecological performance are linked across Earth's biomes.

Location

Global.

Major Taxa Studied

Bacteria and archaea.

Methods

We analysed 576,531 publicly available microbial communities spanning 24 biomes across host-associated and free-living systems worldwide. We developed the Baas-Becking score (BB-score), a taxon-level metric that combines occupancy and relative abundance while penalising absences to quantify relative taxa performance within biomes. Here, the BB-score was applied to data of OTUs with 99% identity cut-off. We then used network analysis to measure biome connectivity based on similarities in their top-performing microbial subcommunities.

Results

Approximately 64% of microbial taxa occurred in both host-associated and free-living biomes, indicating that ecological flexibility across this major lifestyle boundary is common. Biome specialisation was rare, with the highest biome-restricted taxa found in saline biomes. Most microbial taxa emerged as high performers in only a few biomes. By contrast, only a small set of taxa repeatedly ranked among the top performers across many biomes, revealing a strong decoupling between widespread occurrence and high performance. Network analysis of shared high-performing taxa further identified the atmosphere, phyllosphere and freshwater as the main hubs linking Earth's ecosystems.

Main Conclusions

Widespread occurrence does not necessarily indicate high ecological performance in microbes. Instead, global microbial biogeography reflects the combined effects of dispersal and biome-specific performance, with biome connectivity structured by shared high-performing taxa and a small set of hub biomes.
